hook: Mark Chen has been at OpenAI since 2018, moving from quantitative trading into leading some of the company's most visible research programs. He co-led the team that built DALL-E, directed the vision work that gave GPT-4 its multimodal capabilities, and oversaw Codex, the model behind GitHub Copilot. In March 2025 OpenAI named him Chief Research Officer, a role focused on integrating research and product development so new capabilities move into deployment faster. He also coaches the USA Computing Olympiad team, a pastime that tracks with his own path through competitive mathematics and computer science at MIT.

standing.watch: What remains unresolved according to the records is the group of cases against OpenAI entities, all of which are filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. The records do not show any pending case naming Mark Chen himself, and they do not show a planned listing or a dispute involving him personally. The only forward-looking item the records supply is the continued monitoring of those OpenAI dockets. Where the records are thin, they say less: no dates of resolution, no outcomes, and no further detail on his role in the litigation are given.
standing.record: The site's records place Mark Chen as an executive of OpenAI, the San Francisco startup founded in 2015. His background includes a bachelor's degree in mathematics with computer science from MIT in 2012 and work as a quantitative trader at Jane Street Capital building machine-learning models for futures and equities trading before joining OpenAI in 2018. The lawsuits on the site naming OpenAI or its entities include TradeSun, Inc. v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, and Vredenburgh v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, each recorded as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker. One further case, Buist v. Anthropic, PBC, names a different company. The pattern running through the record is that the coverage and cases attach to OpenAI as an institution rather than to Chen personally, and none of the entries records a development beyond filing.
standing.standing: Mark Chen is Chief Research Officer at OpenAI, a position he has held since March 24, 2025, and he has been at the company since 2018. In that role he focuses on integrating research and product development so new capabilities move into deployment faster. The records show he controls or influences research programs that produced DALL-E, the vision work behind GPT-4's image understanding, and Codex, the model underlying GitHub Copilot. OpenAI's own GPT-4 contributions page credits him as Vision team co-lead and Deployment lead, and the o1 contributions page lists him under Leadership and Executive Leadership. He also coaches the USA Computing Olympiad team.
